question: What is the meaning of requirements for product regular updates for functioning in a secure manner in relation to upgradability?
data_point: requirements for product regular updates for functioning in a secure manner
description: The requirements for product regular updates for functioning in a secure manner relate to ensuring that a product can maintain its functionality over time through regular software updates. This is particularly important for products that require frequent updates to function securely, such as electronic devices. The ISO 59040 standard emphasizes the need for public availability of data to support these updates, ensuring that manufacturers can transparently assess the product's ability to meet anticipated future requirements of users. This helps to extend the product's useful life and maintain its desirability over its functional lifetime.

Manual data entry in DPPs can lead to human errors, which signifi-
cantly impact decision-making (Bafandegan Emroozi and Modares,
2024). From Fig. 5, the data source is still manually entered by stake-
holders throughout the supply chain, increasing the likelihood of errors.
Panza et al. (2023) recommended the use of cyber-physical systems for
transferring data to the DPP throughout a product lifecycle, with each
piece of data secured via blockchain. Additionally, manual data entry by
the maintenance service provider can vary from person to person, which
could yield misleading data (including data with incompatible formats
and semantics) that could affect the circularity potential (G¨oswein et al.,
2022). Future efforts should prioritise the development of a standardised
format to facilitate seamless updates, reduce administrative burdens and
data inconsistency. This can helpful when multiple service providers are
involved in maintaining the same product. This is crucial for encour-
aging user acceptance and active contribution (G¨oswein et al., 2022).
Fig. 9 illustrates the scenario where one service provider is verified
and authorised to update a maintenance record. For the case of multiple
service providers maintaining the same product may introduce potential
data conflicts or inconsistencies, mechanisms are needed for conflict
prevention, detection and resolution. In general, conflicts of updates can
be resolved by resolved by blockchain consensus algorithms or doble-
spending prevention techniques during transaction validation. In our
suggested framework, we assign unique transaction identifiers using
product ID and timestamps. If two transactions are conflicting, the
transaction with earlier timestamp will be accepted.
3.3.4. Practical implication
The volume of data required for a DPP throughout the product life-
cycle may increase over time and this could potentially lead to data
fatigue in DPP development (Li and Wang, 2021). The new European
battery regulation states that information such as administrative infor-
mation, geographic location of the battery manufacturing facility,
manufacturing date and expected battery lifetime will be mandatory in
DPPs in 2023 (European Commission, 2023; Wagner et al., 2023). For
example, Berger et al. (2022) identified out 54 data points categorized
into three information levels with four main information categories for
EV batteries. (Çetin et al., 2023) developed a template consisting of 50
data points for developing a material passport for social housing and
building management. In addition to that, the EU Battery Regulation
battery passport will be required from February 2027 onwards, included
around 90 data attributes (Battery Pass, 2023). The new battery regu-
lation highlights the importance of such information in enhancing sus-
tainability, but future efforts should focus on analysing which data is
critical to store on the DPP to avoid information overload.
The willingness of service providers to update maintenance history
to DPP is critical to enhance data completeness from a life cycle point of
view. Focusing on the ease-of-use of the framework can increase service
providers’ willingness to update information in DPPs because complex
data updating process can exhaust users and, as a result, reduce their
willingness to use the framework (Moon et al., 2022). Future initiatives,
for example, reputational incentives that enhance the visibility of ser-
